simple.meaning: תַּעֲרֻבָה (taʻărubâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “suretyship , i.e. (concretely) a pledge.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at 2 Kings 14:14. The surrounding context includes kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to תַּעֲרֻבָה (H8594) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: תַּעֲרֻבָה (taʻărubâh) / H8594 is traced through 2 Kings 14:14, 2 Chronicles 25:24 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H8594. taarubah [ תַּעַרֻבָה ] noun feminine pledge ; — only plural in phrase הַתַּעַרֻבוֺת בְּנֵי 2Kin 14:14 i.e. hostages = 2Chr 25:24 .

occurrences.englishText: He took all the gold and silver, and all the vessels that were found in Yahweh’s house and in the treasures of the king’s house, the hostages also, and returned to Samaria.
He took all the gold and silver, and all the vessels that were found in God’s house with Obed-Edom, and the treasures of the king’s house, the hostages also, and returned to Samaria.
